unions.comment:
Battery-save header fields (SRAM bank 0), owned by the bank $03 save
engine; scoped so unrelated $a0xx literals in other banks stay numeric

0xa030.name: sSaveMasterChecksum
0xa030.note: [16-bit LE] byte-sum of $a038-$a76f (version byte + block directory)

0xa038.name: sSaveFormatVersion
0xa038.note: [8-bit] save layout version byte, always $71; first byte covered by the master checksum

unions.comment:
Global save-flag array (SRAM bank 0), owned by the bank $03 save
engine; scoped so unrelated $a0xx literals in other banks (VRAM-bank-1
copy destinations) stay numeric

0xa040.name: sSaveFlags
0xa040.note: [8 bytes] The 64 global save flags the game actually uses. Test/Set/ClearSaveFlag ($03:$4d8f/$4dbd/$4deb) index this base with d (byte) and mask $80 >> bit, where e = bit << 5; flag number = byte * 8 + bit, and the SAVEFLAG_* constants in constants.inc hold the (byte << 8 | bit << 5) id each call site passes. Layout: bytes $00-$03 are the character-unlock bits, one per character id (CheckCharacterUnlocked $18:$452a tests flag number = char id; ids 0-3 are always unlocked). Byte $01 also carries #9 opening-seen and the unlocks granted by outside events - #10-#13 (Fay, Curt, Mark, Sean) from N64 transfer records, #14/#15 (Sammi, Elden) from the singles/doubles Dream Match. Bytes $02/$03 double as the first twelve minigame-clear flags (#20-#31, Boo Blast through Target Shot), which is why clearing a minigame level unlocks a character: it is the same bit. Byte $04 is per-story-slot (SetStorySlotFlagA #32-#34, SetStorySlotFlagB #36-#38; EraseStorySlotSaveData clears the pair for the erased slot). Bytes $05/$06 continue the minigame-clear run (#40-#54, Fruit Fantasy through Two-On-One; MinigameClearFlagTable_1e lists all 27 in order). Byte $07 is court unlocks (#57 Star, #58 Castle, #59 Tropics, #60 Jungle, #61 Warehouse) plus #62 'N64 records present' and #63, the bank $01 debug-menu toggle. The RetroAchievements Code Notes for $a042/$a043/$a045/$a046/$a047 describe the same bits with their own bit numbering (their 'Bit N' is mask 1 << N, i.e. this engine's bit 7 - N); those names now live on the SAVEFLAG_* constants.

0xa048.name: sSaveFlagsUnused
0xa048.note: [24 bytes] Flags #64-#255. ClearSaveFlagsArea ($03:$4825) zeroes all 32 bytes of the array, but nothing ever sets or tests a flag with a byte index above $07: every immediate id in the ROM is $01xx-$07xx, the computed callers are bounded (character ids stop at $1f, MinigameClearFlagTable_1e stops at #54, UnlockConditionFlagRows_03 at #54), so this half is dead storage.

unions.comment:
Save block directory: 113 16-byte entries (see docs/save_format.md);
entry = valid, SRAM bank, offset, length, checksum, tag

0xa060.name: sSaveBlockDirectory
0xa060.note: [113 x 16 bytes] block directory; +0 valid, +1 SRAM bank, +2 offset word, +4 length word, +6 checksum word, +8 tag (hi,lo)

unions.comment:
Mode-local scratch ($c780-$c78f is reused by each game mode;
only proven consumers are named, sites in other modes stay numeric)

0xc781.name: wCharSelectChar
0xc781.note: [8-bit] Character id under the char-select cursor, looked up from the roster grid at $c7a0 by UpdateCharSelectSelection

0xc782.name: wCharSelectPrevChar
0xc782.note: [8-bit] Character id selected on the previous frame (change detection)

0xc783.name: wCharSelectCol
0xc783.note: [8-bit] Char-select cursor column in the roster grid

0xc784.name: wCharSelectRow
0xc784.note: [8-bit] Char-select cursor row in the roster grid

0xc780.name: wMinigameServeCount
0xc780.note: [16-bit] Serves the minigame has launched. LaunchMinigameServe increments it and derives the ball speed from it (count / 10, capped at $19), so the feed speeds up as the round goes on

0xc782.name: wScorePopupValue
0xc782.note: [16-bit] Points the floating score popup shows; AwardHitScore and the per-minigame scorers store the award here before calling AddToMinigameScore

0xc784.name: wMinigameServeSpeed
0xc784.note: [8-bit] Ball speed LaunchMinigameServe passed to LaunchBall for this serve

0xc785.name: wMinigameServeSlot
0xc785.note: [8-bit] Which serve the tennis machine plays next; the machine hooks advance it by 1 or 2 per point and wrap it, and ApplyMinigameCharTargetFromTable indexes the aim table with it

0xc786.name: wMinigameServeGroup
0xc786.note: [8-bit] wMinigameServeSlot / 3, taken by LaunchMinigameServe and read back by LaunchBall

0xc787.name: wScorePopupTimer
0xc787.note: [8-bit] Frames left on the score popup, seeded with $10 by StartScorePopup; UpdateScorePopup ticks it and also uses it as the popup's rise offset

0xc788.name: wMinigameHitScored
0xc788.note: [8-bit] Set while a hit is being scored; ResetTargetHitState only clears the streak when it finds this clear, which is what keeps a streak alive across the points of one rally

0xc789.name: wMinigameHitStreak
0xc789.note: [8-bit] Consecutive scoring hits, stepped by IncrementCappedCounter (b is the cap). AwardHitScore indexes both a sound table and a score table with it, so a longer streak is worth more and sounds different

0xc78a.name: wTreasureBoxState
0xc78a.note: [8-bit] Treasure Box actor state, stepped by AdvanceTreasureBoxActorState and used by DrawTreasureBoxSprite to pick the frame

0xc78b.name: wDrillGateActive
0xc78b.note: [8-bit] Set while the serve gate is still standing: RecordGateCrossOnServe clears it once the serve has passed through (and records the bit in wDrillGateCrossBits), and QueueDrillMarker1/2 only draw the gate markers while it is set

unions.comment:
Sound-engine WRAM (bank $07), used only by the bank-0 audio driver;
scoped to the driver's code range so the same $d1xx/$d2xx offsets
in other WRAM banks keep their numeric address.
The EXP award screen reuses the same bytes from WRAM bank $06, which the
bank $1a/$1d code selects explicitly with `wram_bank $06`.

0xd100.name: wSndChannels
0xd100.note: [192 bytes] Six 32-byte channel state blocks (channels 0-1 music, 2-5 SFX); the active channel's block is mirrored into HRAM $ffd0 each pass, first word = script pointer ($ffff = idle)

0xd1c0.name: wSndLoopSlots
0xd1c0.note: [72 bytes] Per-channel loop bookkeeping (counter + return pointer per loop level); base resolved by GetChannelLoopSlot

0xd208.name: wSndActiveMask
0xd208.note: [8-bit] Bitmask of channels already serviced/keyed this update pass (AbortIfChannelTriggered tests it; folded into rAUDTERM at the end)

0xd209.name: wSndPanShadow
0xd209.note: [8-bit] Shadow of rAUDTERM: per-channel left/right output enable bits accumulated across channels

0xd20b.name: wSndChannelBits
0xd20b.note: [8-bit] Current channel's stereo output bit-pair (ch1=$11 .. ch4=$88), used for active-channel tracking

0xd20c.name: wSndChannelPanMask
0xd20c.note: [8-bit] Same bit-pair as wSndChannelBits, masked against hSndPanMask to build wSndPanShadow

0xd20d.name: wSndRegBase
0xd20d.note: [8-bit] Current channel's APU register offset (type*5); WriteChannelReg forms rAUD via $ff10+this+reg

0xd20e.name: wSndFrameCounter
0xd20e.note: [8-bit] Free-running update counter; low nibble supplies the vibrato phase in TickVibrato

0xd20f.name: wSndChannelIndex
0xd20f.note: [8-bit] Index (0-5) of the channel currently being updated

0xd212.name: wSndUpdateReqMask
0xd212.note: [8-bit] Pending channel-update request: mask of channels to reconfigure (SetChannelUpdateRequest)

0xd213.name: wSndUpdateReqData
0xd213.note: [8-bit] Value applied by the pending channel-update request (low nibble)

0xd214.name: wSndUpdateReqAck
0xd214.note: [8-bit] Accumulator of channels that have acknowledged the pending update request

0xd215.name: wSndFirstChannel
0xd215.note: [8-bit] Channel index the update pass starts from (normally 0)

0xd217.name: wSndLoadedWaveId
0xd217.note: [8-bit] Wave-pattern id currently loaded into wave RAM (change detection for the wave channel)

0xd218.name: wSndTranspose
0xd218.note: [8-bit] Global transpose added to note ids (cmd $a9 $fe/$f2/$f3)

0xd219.name: wSndWaveReloadPending
0xd219.note: [8-bit] Non-zero to force the wave channel to reload its pattern on the next note

0xd161.name: wExpScreenCharStats
0xd161.note: [2 x 15 bytes] Per-character record the EXP award screen works on, selected by wStoryCharacterSlot (slot 0 at +0, slot 1 at +15). InitExpScreenCharStats fills $d161-$d16f; +8 is the 16-bit total CheckExpLevelUp/Down compare, and DrawExpScreenLevelNumber, DrawExpScreenLevelBar and the SweepExpBarMarker routines read +0 and +3

unions.comment:
Match ball-visuals history ring (WRAM bank 4 only); shared renderer
state, so scoped by the selected WRAM bank plus the bank-$08 renderer.

0xdd00.name: wBallHistory
0xdd00.note: [36 bytes] Ball position-history ring (WRAM bank 4): six 6-byte records [projX word, projY word, tile+8, attr]; UpdateBallVisuals ($5153) shifts it down one record per frame and BuildBallSlot writes the newest at +$1e

unions.comment:
Match ball sprite slots (WRAM bank 4 only), alongside the per-character
$df80+ slots; scoped by the selected WRAM bank plus the bank-$08 renderer.

0xde00.name: wNetBallSlot
0xde00.note: [4 bytes] Match sprite-slot record [tile, attr, screenY, screenX] (WRAM bank 4): ball-at-net marker (tile $4e), drawn after the point resolves when the ball rests within $1e0 of the net (BuildNetBallSlot)

0xde04.name: wBallSlot
0xde04.note: [4 bytes] Match sprite-slot record (WRAM bank 4): the ball, tile picked by height band / off-screen state ($40/$42/$44), gated by wBallSpriteEnabled (BuildBallSlot)

0xde08.name: wBallShadowSlot
0xde08.note: [4 bytes] Match sprite-slot record (WRAM bank 4): ball ground shadow (tile $46) at the ball's height-0 projection, gated by wBallShadowEnabled (BuildBallShadowSlot)

0xde0c.name: wBallTrailSlots
0xde0c.note: [20 bytes] Five match sprite-slot records (WRAM bank 4): ball-trail afterimages (tile = ball tile + 8) fed from the history ring; slots 3-5 only when wBallTrailColor is nonzero (BuildBallTrailSlots)

unions.comment:
Match-engine per-character struct, replicated across WRAM banks 4-7
(bank = character: 4 near-P1, 5 far-P1, 6 near-partner, 7 far-partner).
Same field, different character per bank -- one name each. Scoped by the
provably-selected WRAM bank, plus the match banks $07/$08 whose
callback-reached (jp hl) accesses the dataflow can't prove. Only the
named field offsets render; other $dfxx bytes stay numeric.

variants.context: text-arg fetch buffer (menu banks reuse the idle char struct)

0xdf00.name: wTextArgFetchBuffer
0xdf00.note: [bank 5] Scratch buffer that PushTextArgFetchedString fills (via FetchShortTextToBuffer) with a fetched short-text string, then pushes as a text argument; overlaps the idle far-P1 character struct at $df00

variants.context: match character struct (WRAM banks 4-7, and the match/shot/results banks that address it with the bank already selected)

0xdf00.name: wCharPosX
0xdf00.note: [3 bytes] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): lateral X position, 24-bit fixed point (fraction byte + signed 16-bit integer part)

0xdf03.name: wCharPosDepth
0xdf03.note: [3 bytes] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): depth position (toward/away from net), same 24-bit fixed-point format; the two court sides carry opposite signs

0xdf06.name: wCharPosHeight
0xdf06.note: [3 bytes] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): height above court, same 24-bit fixed-point format (zeroed by SetCharPosAndTarget)

0xdf09.name: wCharServeRole
0xdf09.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): serve/side role code (court-position record byte 4-7); XORed with 2 on the per-point side swap, mapped through the $4fa0 table at point start

0xdf0a.name: wCharCourtPos
0xdf0a.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): court position code (court-position record byte 0-3; XORed with 3 on the tiebreak side-swap)

0xdf0b.name: wCharIndex
0xdf0b.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): character index 0-3 (== WRAM bank - 4); bit 0 set = far side (used by CharPointEndReaction and the edge-arrow sprite)

0xdf0d.name: wCharFacingDesired
0xdf0d.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): desired facing direction, eased toward by wCharFacingShown

0xdf0e.name: wCharFacingShown
0xdf0e.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): displayed facing, eased toward wCharFacingDesired by at most wCharFacingEaseRate per frame ($75c0)

0xdf0f.name: wCharFlags
0xdf0f.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): state flags; bit 2 = airborne (set on jump $6dd5, cleared on landing; selects the shadow slot drawn)

0xdf18.name: wCharState
0xdf18.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): state-machine index (RST00 jumptable at $6a77; set via SetCharState)

0xdf1b.name: wCharSpriteFrame
0xdf1b.note: [3 bytes] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): current sprite frame pointer (hi/lo) + h-flip flag, consumed by DrawCharSprite ($650a)

0xdf1e.name: wCharInputSource
0xdf1e.note: [8-bit] Which input drives this character; ReadCharInput indexes CharInputPtrs with it (pad, CPU and link handlers)

0xdf1f.name: wCharInputBits
0xdf1f.note: [8-bit] Input word ReadCharInput produces: held buttons in the high nibble, newly pressed in the low one (ReadCharPadInput builds it from hPlayerInputFlags and hInputRisingEdge); read with the PADB_* bits

0xdf22.name: wCharObjectBank
0xdf22.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): ROM bank of this character's object definition, animation scripts and frame tables. GetPerspectiveScale banks it in through hRomBank / $2000 and SetCharAnimation and StepCharAnimation pass it to FarReadWordDI. 0 means no object is loaded, which is the test UpdateChar exits on

0xdf40.name: wCharVelX
0xdf40.note: [16-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): X velocity (zeroed on placement and at point end)

0xdf46.name: wCharWalkTargetX
0xdf46.note: [16-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): walk-target X (integer part)

0xdf48.name: wCharWalkTargetDepth
0xdf48.note: [16-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): walk-target depth; MoveCharTowardTarget ($7541) walks toward it, snapping when both deltas < $18 (CheckCharNearTarget $78be)

0xdf53.name: wCharScreenX
0xdf53.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): last projected screen X (BuildCharSpriteSlots $7672)

0xdf54.name: wCharScreenY
0xdf54.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): last projected screen Y

0xdf57.name: wCharPointResult
0xdf57.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): point result from this character's perspective (signed wPointWinLoseFlag)

0xdf68.name: wCharFacingEaseRate
0xdf68.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): max facing change per frame, easing wCharFacingShown toward wCharFacingDesired

0xdf6b.name: wGroundStrokeSpeedIndex
0xdf6b.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): speed-row index (e) into the ShotPlacementData tables for ground strokes (topspin/slice/power variants/neutral); selects bytes 4-5 -> shot speed in LoadShotPlacementEntry

0xdf6c.name: wSmashServeSpeedIndex
0xdf6c.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): speed-row index (e) into ShotPlacementData for the smash and all three serves

0xdf6d.name: wReachSpeedIndex
0xdf6d.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): speed-row index (e) into ShotPlacementData for the reach (smash-range) shot variants

0xdf6e.name: wTopspinPlacementIndex
0xdf6e.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): placement-row index (d) into ShotPlacementData for topspin and serve-topspin; selects bytes 0-3 -> target offsets in LoadShotPlacementEntry

0xdf6f.name: wSlicePlacementIndex
0xdf6f.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): placement-row index (d) into ShotPlacementData for slice and serve-slice

0xdf80.name: wCharSpriteSlot
0xdf80.note: [4 bytes] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): sprite-slot record [tile, attr, screenY, screenX] for the character sprite

0xdf88.name: wCharAirShadowSlot
0xdf88.note: [4 bytes] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): sprite-slot record for the airborne shadow (tiles $50/$52/$54/$56 shrink with jump height; drawn only while wCharFlags bit 2 set)

0xdf8c.name: wCharGroundShadowSlot
0xdf8c.note: [4 bytes] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): sprite-slot record for the standing shadow (tile $58; flicker-transparency while grounded)

0xdf92.name: wLobPlacementIndex
0xdf92.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): placement-row index (d) into ShotPlacementDataLob (set from df91 bit 0)

0xdf93.name: wDropPlacementIndex
0xdf93.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): placement-row index (d) into ShotPlacementDataDrop (set from df91 bit 1)

0xdf96.name: wCharDepthKey
0xdf96.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): draw-order depth key ((depth*8)>>8 + $80); DrawActorsByDepth paints teammates back-to-front

0xdf11.name: wCharShotComboTimer
0xdf11.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): frames left to press a second shot button; BufferShotButtonPress seeds it with 5 on the first press and the state-machine dispatch counts it down

0xdf12.name: wAiActionTimer
0xdf12.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): AI countdown -- the reaction delay AiSetReactionDelay randomises, and the hold time AiServePressToss uses to press and release the toss button

0xdf14.name: wCharShotType
0xdf14.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): resolved SHOTTYPE_* for the swing about to happen, looked up by SelectServeShotType / SelectRallyShotType from the two buffered buttons

0xdf15.name: wCharSwingAnim
0xdf15.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): animation id of the swing SelectForehandBackhand picked; the windup plays it + $08 and the contact phase plays it as-is

0xdf16.name: wCharShotButton1
0xdf16.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): first shot button of the current swing (1 = A, 2 = B), 0 = none. The pair with wCharShotButton2 indexes RallyShotTypeTable0/1, which is how A+B combinations become lobs, drops and power shots

0xdf17.name: wCharShotButton2
0xdf17.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): second shot button, captured while wCharShotComboTimer is still running

0xdf19.name: wCharStatePhase
0xdf19.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): sub-step within wCharState; AdvanceCharStatePhase increments it and each state's phase routine dispatches on it

0xdf1a.name: wAiPhase
0xdf1a.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): sub-step of the AI state machine, advanced by AiAdvancePhase (the AI's own counter, separate from wCharStatePhase)

0xdf21.name: wCharObjectDefId
0xdf21.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): object-definition id SetupCharSpriteFromObjectDef was handed; stored and never read again

0xdf24.name: wCharFrameTablePtr
0xdf24.note: [16-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): pointer (in wCharObjectBank) to the frame graphics table GetPerspectiveScale walks to find a frame's tile data

0xdf26.name: wCharFrameVramDest
0xdf26.note: [16-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): VRAM destination the character's frame tiles are copied to

0xdf28.name: wCharAnimTablePtr
0xdf28.note: [16-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): pointer (in wCharObjectBank) to the object's animation-pointer table; SetCharAnimation indexes it by animation id

0xdf2a.name: wCharAnimScriptBase
0xdf2a.note: [16-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): start of the current animation script, which the $ff (jump) command rewinds to

0xdf2c.name: wCharAnimScriptPtr
0xdf2c.note: [16-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): cursor into the current animation script. Commands are word-sized: < $f0 is [delay, frame], $ff jumps, $fe switches animation, $fb toggles the flip bits of wCharSpriteAttr

0xdf2e.name: wCharAnimId
0xdf2e.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): animation currently playing; SetCharAnimation returns early when asked for the one already running

0xdf2f.name: wCharAnimDelay
0xdf2f.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): frames left on the current animation frame; $ff means hold it indefinitely

0xdf30.name: wCharSpriteDirty
0xdf30.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): sprite bookkeeping flags. Bit 6 = the frame or the facing octant changed, so ReloadCharFacingTiles must upload new tiles; it clears the bit itself

0xdf32.name: wCharFacingOctant
0xdf32.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): facing octant 0-7, derived from wCharFacingShown; picks the tile row and, for octants 2 and 6, the mirrored sprite

0xdf33.name: wCharAnimFrame
0xdf33.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): frame id the animation script last selected

0xdf36.name: wCharTileBase
0xdf36.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): first VRAM tile of this character's sprite, from a per-character-index table

0xdf37.name: wCharSpriteAttr
0xdf37.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): OAM attribute byte for the character. The low three bits are the CGB OBJ palette (wCharIndex + 4) and double as the tile-block index ReloadCharFrameGfx uploads into (& $07, + $08); the high bits are the flip bits the animation script's $fb command toggles, and SetCharAnimation clears them with `and $0f`

0xdf38.name: wCharShadowTablePtr
0xdf38.note: [16-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): pointer (in wCharObjectBank) to the per-frame shadow/scale table GetPerspectiveScale reads

0xdf3a.name: wCharGfxBank
0xdf3a.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): ROM bank holding the character's frame graphics; ReloadCharFrameGfx and LoadCharChargeFlashGfx pass it to the bank $00 far-call vector at $0110

0xdf4b.name: wCharSwingFrames
0xdf4b.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): frames elapsed in the current swing phase, reset when the windup starts and incremented by the windup and contact phases

0xdf4f.name: wCharLastShotButton
0xdf4f.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): shot button already recorded, so BufferShotButtonPress ignores it being held

0xdf50.name: wCharBallReachFlags
0xdf50.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): result of this frame's ball-geometry tests: bit 0 = ball within swing range, bit 1 = inside the contact window, bit 4 = within normal reach (clear selects the stretching shot table). Rebuilt every frame by UpdateCharBallGeometry

0xdf51.name: wCharChargeFlashOn
0xdf51.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): set while the charge flash is playing; cleared when the swing starts or aborts

0xdf94.name: wCharMirrorAttrMask
0xdf94.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): attribute bits XORed into wCharSpriteAttr when the facing octant is 2 or 6, i.e. when the sprite is drawn mirrored

0xdf0c.name: wCharBaseFacing
0xdf0c.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): facing this character returns to for its court position, from CourtPosFacingTable_08; PlaceCharAtBasePosition and UpdateCharFacingOctant measure the displayed facing against it

0xdf10.name: wCharFreezeTimer
0xdf10.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): frames the character is frozen for: UpdateCharStateMachine decrements it and returns without running the state, so nothing moves. SetCharState clears it, and FreezeMinigameOpponentOnReturn sets it to hold the minigame opponent still

0xdf4a.name: wCharAimOffset
0xdf4a.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): aim the player asked for with left/right at the moment of the shot, captured by CaptureServeAim / CaptureShotAim. GetShotAimOffsetForSide and ComputeShotTargetX turn it into the target's lateral offset

0xdf58.name: wAiShotButtons
0xdf58.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): shot buttons the AI decided to press this swing (AiPickServeButtons / AiPickShotButtons); AiPressFirstShotButton and AiPressSecondShotButton feed them into wCharInputBits one at a time

0xdf70.name: wCharReachHeight
0xdf70.note: [16-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): how far above or below the character the ball may be and still be hit; CheckCharBallContact compares |wBallRelCharHeight| against it. Loaded from the character attribute record +$10, minus $10

0xdf72.name: wCharReachX
0xdf72.note: [16-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): lateral reach: CheckCharBallContact compares |wBallRelCharX| * 2 against it. Attribute record +$12

0xdf74.name: wCharSmashJumpSpeed
0xdf74.note: [16-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): upward speed of a jump smash, negated into wCharVelHeight by StartCharSwing. Attribute record +$14, plus $0200

0xdf76.name: wCharDiveSpeed
0xdf76.note: [16-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): lunge speed of a dive, turned into wCharVelX/wCharVelDepth through VectorFromLengthAndAngleRaw at the character's facing. Attribute record +$16

0xdf78.name: wCharId
0xdf78.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): character id InitChar was handed, before RemapExtendedCharId

0xdf79.name: wAiReactionDelayNear
0xdf79.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): base frames the AI waits before reacting when the ball is within normal reach; AiSetReactionDelay adds a 0-3 random and stores wAiActionTimer. Attribute record +$1b

0xdf7a.name: wAiReactionDelayFar
0xdf7a.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): same, for a ball outside normal reach (wCharBallReachFlags bit 4 clear), so a stretching return can be made deliberately slower. Attribute record +$1c

0xdf7b.name: wAiTrackingParam
0xdf7b.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): how the AI chases the ball -- read by AiTrackBallPhase and the baseliner rally state. Attribute record +$1d

0xdf7c.name: wAiAimAwayChance
0xdf7c.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): RNG threshold in AiMaybeAimAwayFromChar: the AI aims away from the opponent when the roll is under it, so a higher value places more shots. Attribute record +$1e

0xdf7d.name: wAiServeStyle
0xdf7d.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): AI serve/shot habit: the low nibble indexes ServePressTossPtrs for the toss timing, and AiPickShotButtons reads it too. Attribute record +$1f

0xdf7e.name: wCharSpriteSetId
0xdf7e.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): character id after RemapExtendedCharId; LookupCharSpriteSet and bank $09's LoadOnCourtCharacterGfx use it to find the sprite bank

0xdf7f.name: wAiPositionStrategy
0xdf7f.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): where the AI stands between shots (0/5 baseline, 1 net, others mid-court); an RST00 jumptable index in AiChooseHomePosition and AiChoosePositionByStrategy. Attribute record +$0f

0xdf90.name: wCharSwingAttrWord
0xdf90.note: [16-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): attribute word read from the character record +$19; StartCharSwing tests bit 7 of the low byte, and bits 0 and 1 of wCharSwingAttrWord + 1 select the lob and drop placement rows

0xdf95.name: wCharExpTier
0xdf95.note: [8-bit] Per-character banked struct (WRAM4-7): character class/tier from attribute record +$18; LookupExpTierForChar reads it on the EXP screen

unions.comment:
HRAM pointer scratch ($ffb0-$ffb3): two 16-bit slots each caller uses for
its own purpose, so only proven consumers are named. Sites outside these
scopes stay numeric -- note that banks $0f/$10 load $ffb0 as the immediate
constant -80, not as an address.

0xffb0.name: hStatDeltaOutPtr
0xffb0.note: [16-bit] ComputeLevelUpStatDeltas: caller-supplied destination the per-stat deltas are written to (hl on entry, spilled at $02:$4a02)

0xffb2.name: hStatDeltaRecordCopy
0xffb2.note: [16-bit] ComputeLevelUpStatDeltas: pointer to the 64-byte stack buffer (add sp, -64 at $02:$4a07) holding the player record copied before LevelUpPlayerRecord, which each stat is then differenced against

0xffb0.name: hSaveEditorCursor
0xffb0.note: [16-bit] SaveSlotDebugEditor: byte offset of the edit cursor into the $d300 save-block buffer, wrapped to $400 by masking the high byte with $03; moved by Func_03_524f, which takes the signed cursor step in c and the value step applied on A in b

unions.comment:
Shared HRAM scratch pool: the serial-link input path, the bank-0
sound driver, the sprite queue and the story actor engine reuse the same
bytes (they never run concurrently). Only proven consumers are named;
sites outside every variant's scope keep the numeric address.

variants.context: serial-link input slots (default: link-aware match/menu code in many banks)

0xffd3.name: hLinkInput
0xffd3.note: [8-bit] Effective external input byte produced by SerialDecodeInput (local/remote merged per link role); also the scripted-input feed for demo/CPU-driven characters

0xffd4.name: hLinkRemoteInput
0xffd4.note: [8-bit] Input byte decoded from the last received link frame

0xffd5.name: hLinkRemoteInputBuf
0xffd5.note: [8-bit] Buffered remote input from the previous exchange (double-buffered on the slave side)

0xffd7.name: hLinkTransferDone
0xffd7.note: [8-bit] Set to 1 by SerialHandler when a byte completes; WaitSerialTransfer spins on it and AdvanceFrame's link wait clears it after pairing it with hVBlankOccurred

0xffd8.name: hLinkExchangeActive
0xffd8.note: [8-bit] Non-zero while a serial block exchange runs (UpdateLinkSession, ResyncLinkSession, ExchangeLinkBlockToWram5 set it; the link menus clear it when done). AdvanceFrame skips the SELECT+START debug single-step while it is set

0xffe3.name: hLinkCursorPage
0xffe3.note: [8-bit] Remote player's cursor page in the link character grid, written beside wMenuCursor2X/Y and read by GetGridSlotFromLinkCursor and the MoveLinkCursor* handlers

0xffd0.name: hSndScriptPtr
0xffd0.note: [16-bit] Current channel's script/state pointer, copied from the channel struct each update (borrows the sprite-queue bytes; RunSoundEngine save/restores them)

0xffd2.name: hSndChannelType
0xffd2.note: [8-bit] Channel type in the low 2 bits (0=square1/sweep, 1=square2, 2=wave, 3=noise); high nibble carries the vibrato depth / note-length index

0xffd3.name: hSndDataPtr
0xffd3.note: [16-bit] Pointer to the current channel's note/command data

0xffd5.name: hSndDataBank
0xffd5.note: [8-bit] ROM bank of the current channel's data (loaded into hRomBank/$2000)

0xffd6.name: hSndToneCtrl
0xffd6.note: [8-bit] Tone control: bits 6-7 duty, bit 4 flag, low nibble = note-length increment paired with hSndLengthAccum

0xffd7.name: hSndLengthAccum
0xffd7.note: [8-bit] Fractional note-length accumulator; hSndToneCtrl's low nibble is added each update and carries a step at $10

0xffd8.name: hSndVolume
0xffd8.note: [8-bit] Current channel volume/envelope value (high nibble = level; envelope steps by $10)

0xffd9.name: hSndPortamentoTimer
0xffd9.note: [8-bit] Portamento/glide countdown; while non-zero the channel slides toward the target note instead of advancing the script (cmd $a7)

0xffda.name: hSndWaveId
0xffda.note: [8-bit] Wave-pattern id for the wave channel (compared with wSndLoadedWaveId); reused as a note/instrument byte on the other channels

0xffdb.name: hSndNoteOffset
0xffdb.note: [8-bit] Signed note offset/detune applied when a note is triggered (bit 7 = active); set by cmd $a4

0xffdc.name: hSndTranspose
0xffdc.note: [8-bit] Per-channel transpose added to note ids (cmd $a9 $f0/$f1/$ff)

0xffdd.name: hSndEnvRate
0xffdd.note: [8-bit] Instrument-envelope sweep speed (high nibble); set with hSndEnvLength by cmd $c0-$cf and consumed by TickInstrumentEnvelope

0xffde.name: hSndEnvLength
0xffde.note: [8-bit] Instrument-envelope sweep length/target; on the wave channel it doubles as a note-length byte

0xffdf.name: hSndEnvPos
0xffdf.note: [8-bit] Current instrument-envelope position, advanced toward hSndEnvLength each update

0xffe0.name: hSndVolSlide
0xffe0.note: [8-bit] Volume-slide state (bit 7 direction, remaining steps in the low bits); set by cmd $b0-$df, ticked by TickVolumeSlide

0xffe2.name: hSndVolSlideTimer
0xffe2.note: [8-bit] Volume-slide countdown to the next step

0xffe3.name: hSndPeriodLo
0xffe3.note: [8-bit] Base period low byte of the current note, saved as the vibrato centre (TickVibrato offsets from it)

0xffe4.name: hSndPeriodHi
0xffe4.note: [8-bit] Shadow of NRx4 (period high + control); bit 5 ($20) is a software note-on marker used to tell whether a note is sounding

0xffe5.name: hSndEcho
0xffe5.note: [8-bit] Echo state: low nibble echo depth (ScaleEchoVolume), high nibble saved volume level; set by cmd $aa

0xffe6.name: hSndPanMask
0xffe6.note: [8-bit] This channel's rAUDTERM left/right output bits, merged into wSndPanShadow; set/swapped by cmd $a5

0xffe8.name: hSndNoteLenTimer
0xffe8.note: [8-bit] Note-length countdown; suppresses vibrato/effects until it reaches 0

0xffe9.name: hSndInstrument
0xffe9.note: [8-bit] Instrument selector: high nibble picks the wave pattern / envelope-pointer table, low nibble the envelope sequence; set by cmd $a8

0xffea.name: hSndEchoTimer
0xffea.note: [8-bit] Echo repeat counter (cmd $aa); note this HRAM byte is hActorPtr under the story-actor variant

0xffeb.name: hSndEchoCtrl
0xffeb.note: [8-bit] Echo control: high nibble enable/count, low nibble note offset

0xffed.name: hSndLoopReturnPtr
0xffed.note: [16-bit] Saved script pointer for the active loop (cmd $ac/$ad)

0xffef.name: hSndRestFlag
0xffef.note: [8-bit] Non-zero when the current step is a rest/tie; suppresses the volume envelope in ApplyChannelEnvelope

0xffd0.name: hSpriteBlitY
0xffd0.note: [8-bit] Screen Y origin of the multi-sprite block being queued (QueueSprite32x32)

0xffd1.name: hSpriteBlitX
0xffd1.note: [8-bit] Screen X origin of the multi-sprite block being queued

0xffea.name: hActorPtr
0xffea.note: [16-bit] Pointer to the actor struct currently being processed (stashed around GetActorStateAddr / StepActorScript)

unions.comment:
Screen-local scratch in WRAM bank $03, low half. Like the $d810 block above
each full-screen UI reuses these bytes, so the variants are scoped to the
owning ROM bank (and, where one bank runs several screens, to that screen's
code range).

0xd800.name: wEquipItemList
0xd800.note: [8 bytes] Item ids the player owns, compacted by BuildOwnedItemList from wEquipOwnedMap; the cursor indexes this list

0xd808.name: wEquipOwnedMap
0xd808.note: [8 bytes] One byte per item slot: 0 not owned, 1 owned, 2 owned and equipped. MarkOwnedRackets / MarkOwnedShoes fill it from the save data

0xd800.name: wNameEntryBuffer
0xd800.note: [8 bytes] Name being typed, terminated by $00; AppendCharToName / DeleteLastNameChar edit it and RunNameEntryScreen copies it into the character record on accept ($de is the blank-cell filler)

0xd800.name: wResultScreenWon
0xd800.note: [8-bit] 1 if the player won the match just played, 0 if not; written beside wResultScreenMode by RunMatchWinLoseScreen and used by LoadWinLoseScreenAssets / LoadResultScreenTileGraphics to pick the graphics set

0xd801.name: wResultScreenMode
0xd801.note: [8-bit] Stored from a by RunMatchWinLoseScreen and RunMatchStatsScreen; SetWinLosePortraitPaletteAttrs and LoadResultPortraitSlot branch on it

0xd800.name: wRankingBoardDoubles
0xd800.note: [8-bit] Nonzero shows the doubles ranking rather than the singles one; ShowRankingBoard takes it from b, and it picks both the screen asset record and Draw/HighlightSinglesRankingRows vs the doubles pair

0xd801.name: wRankingBoardPlayerRow
0xd801.note: [8-bit] Which ranking row is the player's, from c; the highlight and the marker animation address the board through it

0xd802.name: wRankingBoardMode
0xd802.note: [8-bit] How the board is presented, from d: 0 plain, 1 plays fanfare $2b, 2 plays the second fanfare and registers RankingCursorBobTask. A 3 is turned back into 0 with w3_d85a set instead

0xd803.name: wRankingMarkerSlots
0xd803.note: [8-bit] Base of the ranking marker slots (83 bytes, $d803-$d855, so it runs past this block into the $d810 one). Cleared by ClearRankingMarkerSlots and filled by LoadRankingMarkerCoords; GetRankingMarkerSlot hands out one per marker drawn

0xd801.name: wDataScreenPage
0xd801.note: [8-bit] Page the bank $3b data screens are showing; DrawN64TnmtPageLabels and the bracket builders key off it and N64TnmtScrollArrowsTask decides from it which scroll arrows to draw

0xd802.name: wDataScreenCursorRow
0xd802.note: [8-bit] Cursor row within the page, stepped by ScrollN64TnmtDataCursor

0xd801.name: wTitleSpriteFrame
0xd801.note: [8-bit] Frame of the title screen's animated sprite; QueueTitleSprite reads it and StepTitleSpriteAnimation advances it

0xd802.name: wTitleSpriteTimer
0xd802.note: [8-bit] Frames left on the current title sprite frame

variants.context: screen scratch (any other screen, where WRAM bank $03 is provable)

0xd800.name: wScreenScratch
0xd800.note:
[8-bit] Base of the screen-local scratch block in WRAM bank $03. Screens
with no named variant here still use it as their working buffer -- an
object array (bank $18), a decompression staging area (banks $1b/$39), a
cursor or mode byte (banks $3b/$6b) -- so this only records where the
block starts. Sites whose WRAM bank compute_wram_bank cannot prove keep
the bare address.

unions.comment:
Rules-screen animation state (WRAM bank $03), owned by the bank $17
rules screen.

0xdc00.name: wRulesScreenAnimFrame
0xdc00.note: [8-bit] Frame AdvanceRulesScreenAnimFrame steps; DrawRulesScreenCharacters indexes RulesScreenCharactersTable0-2 with it

unions.comment:
Screen-local state in WRAM bank $03: each full-screen UI reuses these
bytes for its own purpose, so the variants are scoped to the ROM bank
that owns the screen rather than to the WRAM bank -- banks $16/$17/$38
all select WRAM bank $03 here, and most sites select it in a callee so
compute_wram_bank cannot prove it at the reference.

0xd810.name: wBriefingPlayerX
0xd810.note: [8-bit] Drill-briefing diagram: player sprite X, queued by DrawBriefingPlayerSprite (d = X, e = Y in QueueSprite)

0xd812.name: wBriefingOpponentX
0xd812.note: [8-bit] Drill-briefing diagram: opponent sprite X, queued by DrawBriefingOpponentSprite

0xd814.name: wBriefingSwingX
0xd814.note: [8-bit] Drill-briefing diagram: swing-animation sprite X, queued by DrawBriefingSwingAnim

0xd816.name: wBriefingSpinMarkerX
0xd816.note: [8-bit] Drill-briefing diagram: spin-serve marker X, queued by DrawSpinServeBriefingMarker

0xd818.name: wBriefingRotMarkerX
0xd818.note: [8-bit] Drill-briefing diagram: rotatable marker X, queued by DrawBriefingMarkerRotated

0xd81a.name: wBriefingPole1X
0xd81a.note: [8-bit] Drill-briefing diagram: first pole sprite X, queued by DrawBriefingPoleSprites

0xd81b.name: wBriefingPole1Y
0xd81b.note: [8-bit] Drill-briefing diagram: first pole sprite Y

0xd81c.name: wBriefingHMarkerX
0xd81c.note: [8-bit] Drill-briefing diagram: horizontal marker X, queued by DrawBriefingMarkerHFlip (jiggles by 1px on hVBlankCounter bit 4)

0xd81e.name: wBriefingBallX
0xd81e.note: [8-bit] Drill-briefing diagram: ball sprite X, queued by DrawBriefingBallSprite

0xd820.name: wBriefingPole2X
0xd820.note: [8-bit] Drill-briefing diagram: second pole sprite X (same drawer as wBriefingPole1X)

0xd821.name: wBriefingPole2Y
0xd821.note: [8-bit] Drill-briefing diagram: second pole sprite Y

0xd822.name: wBriefingSwingFrame
0xd822.note: [8-bit] Drill-briefing diagram: swing-animation frame (0-9); indexes BriefingSwingAnimTable0 for the base tile, and < 6 selects the 5-sprite racket template

0xd823.name: wBriefingVMarkerX
0xd823.note: [8-bit] Drill-briefing diagram: vertical marker X, queued by DrawBriefingMarkerVFlip

0xd825.name: wBriefingVMarkerUpright
0xd825.note: [8-bit] Drill-briefing diagram: 1 draws the vertical marker upright (OAM attr $09), anything else Y-flipped ($49)

0xd826.name: wBriefingSpinMarkerUnflipped
0xd826.note: [8-bit] Drill-briefing diagram: 1 draws the spin-serve marker unflipped (OAM attr $09), anything else X-flipped ($29)

0xd827.name: wBriefingRotMarkerDir
0xd827.note: [8-bit] Drill-briefing diagram: rotatable marker orientation (0-3); indexes BriefingMarkerRotatedTable, the four flip combinations of OAM attr $x9

0xd828.name: wBriefingBracketX
0xd828.note: [8-bit] Drill-briefing diagram: target-bracket top-left X; DrawBriefingTargetBrackets draws the four corners at X, X+width+3

0xd829.name: wBriefingBracketY
0xd829.note: [8-bit] Drill-briefing diagram: target-bracket top-left Y; corners sit at Y and Y+height-5

0xd82a.name: wBriefingBracketWidth
0xd82a.note: [8-bit] Drill-briefing diagram: target-bracket width in pixels (corner offset is width+3)

0xd82b.name: wBriefingBracketHeight
0xd82b.note: [8-bit] Drill-briefing diagram: target-bracket height in pixels (corner offset is height-5)

0xd82c.name: wBriefingAnimTimer
0xd82c.note: [8-bit] Drill-briefing animation frame timer; each briefing's *_TickAnim increments it and calls *_AdvanceAnim at $78 (120 frames)

0xd82d.name: wBriefingHMarkerUnflipped
0xd82d.note: [8-bit] Drill-briefing diagram: 1 draws the horizontal marker unflipped (OAM attr $09), anything else X-flipped ($29)

0xd82e.name: wBriefingAnimStep
0xd82e.note: [8-bit] Drill-briefing animation step; each briefing's *_AdvanceAnim wraps it (and a & $03) and indexes its 4-byte-per-step position table with it

0xd830.name: wBriefingTargetPalette
0xd830.note: [8 bytes] Drill-briefing target palette scratch: CycleDiagramTargetPaletteData copied here, colour 2 ($d834) replaced with the cycling colour, then uploaded by LoadPaletteShadow

0xd811.name: wCharGridPage
0xd811.note: [8-bit] Character-select grid: top row currently shown (wMenuCursorX/Y address the cell within it); MoveCharGridCursor* wrap it and rebuild the page sprite list

0xd812.name: wCharGridPageCount
0xd812.note: [8-bit] Character-select grid: number of pages, looked up from wCharGridEntryCount through CharGridPageCountTable

0xd813.name: wCharSelectMode
0xd813.note: [8-bit] Character-select mode id stored on entry by RunExhibitionCharSelectScreen / RunLinkCharSelectScreen; picks the slot-box table and the starting slot (3 and 5 start at slot 2)

0xd814.name: wCharSelectSlot
0xd814.note: [8-bit] Character-select: player slot being chosen (0-3); $04 means every slot is filled and the screen shows the wait banner

0xd815.name: wCharSelectExitCode
0xd815.note: [8-bit] Character-select result polled by the frame loop: 0 keep running, 1 finished, 2 cancelled out

0xd816.name: wCharSelectSlotChars
0xd816.note: [4 bytes] Character id chosen for each player slot ($ff = empty); ResolveSelectedCharIds and InitMatchCharsFromSelection read it

0xd81a.name: wCharGridEntryCount
0xd81a.note: [8-bit] Character-select grid: roster entries present from $da24 on (CountCharGridEntries)

0xd81b.name: wCharGridPrevPage
0xd81b.note: [8-bit] Character-select grid: page saved when a left/right wrap jumps to the roster pages

0xd81c.name: wCharGridBuilt
0xd81c.note: [8-bit] Set to 1 by BuildCharGridFromUnlockFlags once the grid has been populated

0xd81d.name: wCharSelectRemoteSlot
0xd81d.note: [8-bit] Link character-select: slot the remote player is choosing; Advance/RetreatRemotePlayerSlot step it

0xd81f.name: wCharSelectRemoteChars
0xd81f.note: [2 bytes] Link character-select: character ids the remote player has locked in (slots 2 and 3)

0xd821.name: wLinkSelectCmdChar
0xd821.note: [8-bit] Link character-select: character id carried by the last received select command

0xd822.name: wLinkSelectSlotState
0xd822.note: [8-bit] Link character-select slot bookkeeping, reset when a selection is retreated

0xd823.name: wCharGridCreatedCount
0xd823.note: [8-bit] Character-select grid: entries present in the nine created-character rows at $da00 (counted alongside wCharGridEntryCount)

0xd824.name: wCpuDifficultyPrompt
0xd824.note: [8-bit] Set when the slot just filled needs the CPU-difficulty submenu; the frame loop runs RunCpuDifficultySubmenu instead of normal input while it is set

0xd825.name: wCpuDifficultyPanelOpen
0xd825.note: [8-bit] Set once OpenCpuDifficultyPanel has drawn the panel, so the submenu only opens it on the first pass

0xd826.name: wCpuDifficultyCursor
0xd826.note: [8-bit] Cursor value in the CPU-difficulty submenu; stored into wCharSelectSlotDifficulty on confirm

0xd830.name: wCharSelectSlotDifficulty
0xd830.note: [4 bytes] CPU difficulty chosen per player slot; ApplyCpuDifficultyToCharRecords copies it into the match character records

0xd834.name: wCharSelectSlotStar
0xd834.note: [4 bytes] Star-character flag per player slot; ApplyStarFlagsToCharRecords copies it to $ca0e/$ca4e/$ca8e/$cace

0xd838.name: wLinkSelectCmdResult
0xd838.note: [8-bit] Link character-select: result byte ProcessLinkSelectCommand leaves for commands $24-$27

0xd839.name: wLinkCpuDifficulty
0xd839.note: [8-bit] Link character-select: CPU difficulty for the link match, stepped by HandleLinkCpuDifficultyInput

0xd820.name: wWindowId
0xd820.note: [8-bit] Window struct index AllocWindowStruct handed out for the window being built, $ff when none was free; CreateMenuWindowFromText passes it to SetWindowTextId / SetWindowState and returns it

0xd824.name: wDialogueWindowId
0xd824.note: [8-bit] Window struct index of the dialogue window currently on screen, stored by CreateDialogueWindow. RedrawActiveTextWindow, RenderActiveWindowText, CloseActiveDialogueWindow and the speaker-dialogue helpers all address the window through it

0xd825.name: wDialogueWindowCol
0xd825.note: [8-bit] Dialogue window top-left tilemap column (wrapped to $1f)

0xd826.name: wDialogueWindowRow
0xd826.note: [8-bit] Dialogue window top-left tilemap row (wrapped to $1f)

0xd827.name: wDialogueWindowHeight
0xd827.note: [8-bit] Dialogue window height in cells, from b at CreateDialogueWindow

0xd828.name: wDialogueWindowWidth
0xd828.note: [8-bit] Dialogue window width in cells, from c at CreateDialogueWindow

0xd829.name: wTextRedrawGuard
0xd829.note: [8-bit] Re-entrancy guard around RedrawActiveTextWindow: the delay/wait text commands only redraw while it is 0, and set it for the duration of their own redraw

0xd82f.name: wMenuWindowId
0xd82f.note: [8-bit] Window struct index of the menu window CreateMenuWindowFromText just built (a copy of wWindowId taken as the menu is pushed)

0xd830.name: wMenuCursorRow
0xd830.note: [8-bit] Row the menu cursor sits on; RunMenuSelection steps it against wMenuRowCount and returns it as the chosen entry

0xd831.name: wMenuRowCount
0xd831.note: [8-bit] Number of selectable rows in the current menu, derived from MeasureTextDimensions ((lines - 1) / 2)

0xd832.name: wMenuStack
0xd832.note: [12 bytes] Six two-byte frames, one per nested menu, indexed by wMenuDepth * 2: [wMenuRowCount << 4 | saved wMenuCursorRow, window id]. Pushed by CreateMenuWindowFromText and unwound when a menu is cancelled

0xd83e.name: wMenuDepth
0xd83e.note: [8-bit] Number of menus currently stacked; indexes wMenuStack

0xd821.name: wGlyphWindowId
0xd821.note: [8-bit] Window struct index the glyph stream is rendering into, set by RedrawWindowText / RenderWindowTextToCompletion. InitGlyphStreamForWindow, DrawWindowGlyphRun, FlushGlyphRow and UploadLastGlyphTiles all resolve the window through it

0xd810.name: wEquipItemCount
0xd810.note: [8-bit] Number of entries BuildOwnedItemList put in wEquipItemList

0xd811.name: wEquipEquippedIndex
0xd811.note: [8-bit] Index within wEquipItemList of the item currently equipped (the slot BuildOwnedItemList saw marked 2)

0xd812.name: wEquipSelectExitTimer
0xd812.note: [8-bit] 0 while the screen is running; once a choice is made it counts up each frame and the screen fades out at $14

0xd813.name: wEquipItemKind
0xd813.note: [8-bit] 0 = rackets, 1 = shoes; selects the icon set, the info panel and which stat-modifier table GetItemStatModListPtr reads

0xd814.name: wEquipStatRowSet
0xd814.note: [8-bit] Which row-address table GetStatModRowAddr uses for the stat-modifier panel; both loaders set it to 0

0xd810.name: wStatsPrintBuffer
0xd810.note: [8 bytes] Digit scratch PrintSinglesMatchStats / PrintDoublesMatchStats hand to PrintNumberRightAligned as bc while writing each stat into the shadow tilemap

unions.comment:
Character-data (level-up) screen working set, WRAM bank $06, shared by
the bank $1a/$1c/$1d screen code. The first four bytes are a smaller
scratch that three screens overlay -- the debug character viewer, the
results continue prompt and the character-data screen itself -- so those
get their own range-scoped variants ahead of it.

0xd004.name: wCharViewerPalette
0xd004.note: [8-bit] Palette index the debug character viewer is showing, from GetCharPaletteIndex

0xd005.name: wCharViewerPose
0xd005.note: [8-bit] Animation/pose index the debug character viewer is showing, stepped by RunCharViewerInputLoop

0xd000.name: wCharViewerRow
0xd000.note: [8-bit] Which row of the debug character viewer the cursor is on, toggled with `xor $01`: 0 = the character grid, 1 = the palette row

0xd001.name: wCharViewerCursor
0xd001.note: [8-bit] Cursor index within the current row; up/down step it by $0b, the grid width

0xd002.name: wCharViewerCharId
0xd002.note: [8-bit] Character the viewer is showing, chosen by RunCharViewerSelectGrid and turned into wCharViewerPalette by GetCharPaletteIndex

0xd003.name: wCharViewerSavedCursor
0xd003.note: [8-bit] Grid cursor saved while the palette row has focus, so switching rows comes back to the same character

0xd000.name: wContinuePromptKind
0xd000.note: [8-bit] Which continue prompt is up, stored from c by InitResultsPromptState

0xd001.name: wContinuePromptRow
0xd001.note: [8-bit] Cursor row, toggled 0/1 by up and down; picks which of the two cursor sprites DrawContinuePromptCursor queues

0xd002.name: wContinuePromptPage
0xd002.note: [8-bit] Which page of the prompt text is showing (RefreshContinuePromptText)

0xd003.name: wContinuePromptResult
0xd003.note: [8-bit] What the prompt returned: 1 confirm, $ff cancel, or wContinuePromptPage - 1

0xd004.name: wCharDataLevel
0xd004.note: [8-bit] Level the character-data screen is committing; WriteCharStatsToDisplayBuffer stores it back into record +$18 (wStoryModeMainCharacterLevel)

0xd005.name: wCharDataNewLevels
0xd005.note: [4 bytes] Spin/Power/Control/Speed levels the screen is committing; WriteCharStatsToDisplayBuffer stores them back into record +$38-$3b

0xd009.name: wCharDataPointsLeft
0xd009.note: [8-bit] Unspent level-up points on the character-data screen, copied in from $d003 and decremented by CharDataScreen_InputLoop after each LevelUpPlayer

0xd00a.name: wCharDataLevels
0xd00a.note: [4 bytes] Spin/Power/Control/Speed levels as loaded from record +$38-$3b (LoadCharStats / LoadCharStatsWithLevelUpDeltas)

0xd00e.name: wCharDataStats
0xd00e.note: [11 bytes] The eleven displayed stats, loaded from record +$20-$2a with 1 added to each (Top, Slice, Serve, Stroke, Volley, Angle, Placement, Speed, Dash, Reaction, Stop -- the order of wStoryModeMainCharacterTopStat onwards)

0xd019.name: wCharDataStatDeltas
0xd019.note: [11 bytes] Per-stat change the pending level-up would apply, filled by ComputeLevelUpStatDeltas (or cleared when wCharDataPage is $04); DrawStatArrowIndicators turns each into an up/down arrow beside its stat

0xd024.name: wCharDataPage
0xd024.note: [8-bit] Which of the four level-up choices the cursor is on, or $04 for the confirm cell; CharDataScreen_DrawPageColumns and DrawStatValueSprites both key off it

0xd025.name: wCharDataConfirmState
0xd025.note: [8-bit] Step of the confirm prompt (RunCharDataConfirmScreen); DrawCharDataPromptCursor draws the cursor from it

0xd026.name: wCharDataRevealTimer
0xd026.note: [8-bit] AnimateCharDataStatsReveal countdown between stat rows; CharDataScreen_InitState seeds it with $0a

0xd027.name: wCharDataRevealStep
0xd027.note: [8-bit] AnimateCharDataStatsReveal step; CharDataScreen_InitState seeds it with $03

0xd028.name: wCharDataLevelPreview
0xd028.note: [8-bit] 0 while the allocation page is live: DrawStatValueSprites then draws the level one higher, in palette $0f, to preview the level about to be gained. CharDataScreen_InitState sets it to $03 on re-entry and CharDataScreen_Show clears it

0xd029.name: wCharDataChoiceCount
0xd029.note: [8-bit] Number of entries written to wCharDataChoiceLog so far; also the write index

unions.comment:
Character-data level-up log (WRAM bank $06). ComputeTrophyExpForGroup in
bank $1e uses one byte inside the same range for its own accumulator, so
it keeps the variant it had; the log covers the rest.

0xd038.name: wTrophyExpGroup
0xd038.note: [8-bit] Character group being totalled; indexes TrophyExpForGroupTable0-4 and selects the row GetTrophyExpValue reads

0xd02a.name: wCharDataChoiceLog
0xd02a.note: [100 bytes] One byte per level-up taken on this visit: the wCharDataPage the player confirmed. Cleared by WriteCharStatsToDisplayBuffer before the screen opens

unions.comment:
Overworld actor engine scratch (WRAM bank $04), owned by the bank $04
actor-script VM. Scoped to that bank as well as to the WRAM bank: the
VM selects the bank once on entry, so most references cannot prove it.

0xdaea.name: wPlayerMoveAngle
0xdaea.note: [8-bit] Heading the D-pad asks the overworld player to walk in ($40 per quarter turn, matching the FACE_* encoding). UpdatePlayerControl also writes it to actor field +$34, then probes $20/$40/$e0/$c0 away from it to slide along a blocked wall

0xdaec.name: wPlayerMoveAngleApplied
0xdaec.note: [8-bit] Heading actually walked this frame, 0 when the move was blocked

0xdaed.name: wPlayerMoveAnglePrev
0xdaed.note: [8-bit] Previous frame's wPlayerMoveAngleApplied, saved before it is recomputed

0xdaee.name: wPlayerMoving
0xdaee.note: [8-bit] Cleared when no direction is held, so the walk animation stops

0xdaf7.name: wActorScriptBank
0xdaf7.note: [8-bit] ROM bank of the actor script currently executing, taken from the actor's field +$22. Every ActorScriptOp_* passes it to FarReadByte / FarReadWord / CallHLInBankA to reach the script bytes

unions.comment:
Story-script scratch, second half ($c2b0-$c2bf as a whole is the
current location's scratch block; wMapSceneStage and wMapSceneStage2
are its first two bytes). Two consumers overlay it: bank $14's island
cutscenes keep two sprite slots here as parallel byte arrays, and bank
$15's water-sprite swing contest keeps 16-bit counters over the same
bytes. The three wWaterSpriteMinigame* names that used to sit here in
ram_map.json were global, so they also labelled the generic scratch use
in banks $0e/$0f/$10/$13, which is what STATUS flagged as mis-scoped.

0xc2b2.name: wCutsceneObjX
0xc2b2.note: [2 bytes] World X of cutscene sprite slot 0 and slot 1; the drawers subtract hScrollX to get the OAM X. The plane sequence has no second object and borrows slot 0's byte as its frame counter (AdvancePlaneFrameCounter_14)

0xc2b4.name: wCutsceneObjY
0xc2b4.note: [2 bytes] World Y of the two cutscene sprite slots

0xc2b6.name: wCutsceneObjPhase
0xc2b6.note: [2 bytes] Animation phase of each slot: the splash's rise/fall step and the firework's burst step, both used to index the frame tables

0xc2b8.name: wCutsceneObjTimer
0xc2b8.note: [2 bytes] Per-slot frame timer -- the splash's hit counter (0-8) and the firework's countdown to the next burst frame

0xc2ba.name: wCutsceneObjLimit
0xc2ba.note: [2 bytes] Per-slot phase limit, rerolled from the RNG when a splash respawns

0xc2bc.name: wCutsceneObjRiseTimer
0xc2bc.note: [2 bytes] Frames left in the rise, counted down by AdvanceWaterSplash0Rise_14 / AdvanceWaterSplash1Rise_14, which also lift wCutsceneObjY by 2 each frame

0xc2be.name: wCutsceneObjActive
0xc2be.note: [2 bytes] Per-slot active flag; 0 means the object is still rising and the hit test is skipped

0xc2b4.name: wSwingContestTimer
0xc2b4.note: [16-bit] Frames left in the swing contest; WaterSpriteSwingCountTask counts it down and ends the contest at 0

0xc2b6.name: wSwingContestSwings
0xc2b6.note: [16-bit] Swings counted so far, incremented on each A/B press and printed by PrintHexWord as the contest runs

0xc2b8.name: wSwingContestPrevInput
0xc2b8.note: [8-bit] A/B rising edge from the previous frame, so one press counts once

0xc2b9.name: wSwingContestSwingState
0xc2b9.note: [8-bit] 2 once a swing has been registered, 1 on the frame after -- which is how the swing animation is triggered exactly once

0xc2bb.name: wSwingContestHudPage
0xc2bb.note: [8-bit] Which HUD page the swing contest shows; InitWaterSpriteMinigameHud seeds it and QueueWaterSpriteMinigameHudPanels queues the panels for it

unions.comment:
Screen tilemap buffer, WRAM bank $03. The full-screen UIs assemble
their BG map here and QueueVRAMCopy it to $9800; wShadowTilemapBank /
wShadowTilemapPtr point the text engine at it. Rows are $20 cells
apart, so a cell is $d000 + row * $20 + column -- which is why so many
$d0xx-$d3xx addresses in the screen banks are literal cell addresses
and stay numeric. Only the base is named.

variants.context: screen tilemap (any bank, where WRAM bank $03 is provable)

0xd000.name: wShadowTilemap
0xd000.note: [8-bit] First cell of the screen tilemap buffer ($d000-$d3ff, 32 x 32 cells). The attribute plane is the same offset in the WRAM bank the screen pairs with it (bank $02 for the screens that upload to $b800)
